S067.name: Preoccupation_with_Appearance
S067.description: Preoccupation with one or more perceived defects or flaws in physical appearance that are not observable or appear slight to others.

subtypes.Skin Defects: Excessive preoccupation with practically invisible acne, scars, or complexion.
subtypes.Facial Features: Preoccupation with the shape or size of the nose, eyes, or mouth, which appear normal to others.
subtypes.Asymmetry: Excessive obsession with the face or body not being perfectly symmetrical.
subtypes.Muscle Dysmorphia: The belief that one's body is too small or insufficiently muscular despite being normal or muscular.
subtypes.Specific Body Parts: Obsession that specific parts like hair, teeth, or chest are ugly or abnormal.

S068.name: Appearance_Related_Repetitive_Behaviors
S068.description: Repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed in response to appearance concerns.

subtypes.Mirror Checking or Avoidance: Compulsively checking oneself in the mirror frequently or, conversely, avoiding mirrors strictly.
subtypes.Excessive Camouflaging: Spending excessive time and effort to hide perceived flaws using makeup, clothes, hats, or sunglasses.
subtypes.Skin Picking: Picking or manipulating the skin excessively to remove or 'fix' flaws.
subtypes.Reassurance Seeking: Repetitively asking others for confirmation that one's appearance is okay or not strange.
subtypes.Comparing: Constantly comparing one's body parts with those of passersby or celebrities.
subtypes.Seeking Cosmetic Procedures: Repeatedly seeking or receiving plastic surgery or dermatological procedures.

symptom.disease_info: Body Dysmorphic Disorder (BDD) is characterized by a persistent preoccupation with perceived defects or flaws in physical appearance that are either not observable or appear minor to others, leading to significant distress or functional impairment. Individuals typically engage in repetitive behaviors or mental acts (such as checking, grooming, comparing, or seeking reassurance) in response to these concerns. Onset is often in adolescence or early adulthood, and the course tends to be chronic, with symptoms waxing and waning in intensity, frequently associated with shame, avoidance, and ideas of reference about being judged for one’s looks. BDD is distinguished from normal appearance concerns by the intensity of preoccupation, time consumed, and functional impairment, and from eating disorders by its focus on specific body features rather than weight or shape alone.

patient.personality: Shauna is a warm, socially energetic, and spontaneous organizer who loves bringing people together through community activities, cooking, and creative hobbies.
patient.stressor: Shauna first became unusually focused on her appearance after a minor fall two years ago left a small facial bruise and swelling that her doctor and family assured her would heal without consequence. Around the same time, she began noticing age-related changes—thinning hair, looser skin, and weight shifts—that contrasted sharply with old photographs she used for her digital scrapbooks and senior‑center presentations. As she continued leading wellness classes and hosting potlucks, she started paying increasing attention to how she might look in photos and in front of her groups, gradually spending more and more time preparing herself before any social activity and feeling hesitant to join spontaneous outings unless she could "fix" perceived flaws. Over months, this preoccupation began to interfere with her leadership roles and day trips with friends, and her husband and book club members finally encouraged her to seek psychiatric help when they noticed she was repeatedly delaying or canceling plans because she felt she had to keep adjusting how she looked before leaving the house.
patient.chief_complaint: “I keep fussing over my face and hair for so long before I go anywhere that it’s starting to make me late or skip things altogether.”

S067.name: Preoccupation_with_Appearance
S067.description: Preoccupation with one or more perceived defects or flaws in physical appearance that are not observable or appear slight to others.
S067.manifestation: Ever since that fall, I can’t stop staring at this spot on my cheek and the sagging around my jaw in every photo or mirror, and even though my husband and the ladies at the senior center swear they don’t see anything, all I can think is that everyone notices how lopsided and worn-out my face looks now compared to the old pictures I use in my scrapbooks and presentations.

S068.name: Appearance_Related_Repetitive_Behaviors
S068.description: Repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed in response to appearance concerns.
S068.manifestation: Before every potluck or wellness class, I end up standing in the bathroom for an hour or more, blow‑drying and rearranging my thinning hair, dabbing makeup over the same tiny patch on my cheek, changing my blouse again and again, and asking my poor husband, “Are you sure it doesn’t look terrible?” until I either show up late or call to say I’m not feeling up to coming at all.
